doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

chapter: Opinions on jazz and big bands
title: Bebop in the press in the late 1940s
summary: Press then was about the big bands' decline; Dizzy and Parker appear only in the 1950s.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: When you came back from the war did you notice, did you sense this bebop thing happening? Was it in the musical press that you can remember, like Down Beat and all this in the late 40s?
Okay. I’m just trying to get a sense of —

I think in the ‘50s yeah, but in the late ‘40’s no. The press had to do mostly with the downfall of the big bands. And I guess Dizzy got some press. But if you look at the Down Beat and Metronome contest for the musician of the year you won’t find Dizzy in those years. You will in the 50s, you’ll find Dizzy and Charlie Parker and people like that. And they’re good musicians, they really are, those guys. I just don’t understand some of the things they do.
